questions.question: Buses must never carry:
questions.explanation: Buses can carry some hazardous materials under certain rules. However, tear gas and irritating materials are never allowed. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D and emergency medical supplies are permitted.

questions.question: If a driver must leave a school bus to check that all students have boarded, the driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine and take the key.
Ask another bus driver to watch the bus.
Ask all students to exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine and take the key.
questions.explanation: If the driver cannot see all students boarding, the driver should turn off the engine, take the key, and then check around and under the bus.

questions.question: While students board and leave the bus, the driver should:

options.text: Watch the students and pay attention to what they are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the students and pay attention to what they are doing.
questions.explanation: The driver must watch students as they board and exit. Make sure students do not get caught in doors or handrails. Also check that students move to a safe distance after they exit the bus.

questions.question: A bus driver:

options.text: Does not need to wear a seat belt, but it is a good idea.
Should not wear a seat belt.
Must wear a seat belt only if licensed for less than a year.

questions.explanation: The driver's seat on a bus has a seat belt. The driver must always wear it.

questions.question: Bus accidents happen most often:
questions.explanation: Most bus accidents happen at intersections. Be extra careful when driving through intersections where there are many vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:

options.text: You should use only the parking brake to stop.
You should stop driving and wait for the ABS to start working again.

questions.explanation: The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) works together with your regular brakes. It stops the brakes from locking up during hard braking. If the ABS breaks, your regular brakes will still work. You can drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Buses must never carry:

options.text: Any amount of solid Class 6 poisons.

questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry radioactive materials. Buses also cannot carry Division 2.3 poison gas, liquid Class 6 poisons, tear gas, or irritating materials.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:

options.text: Skip stairs and take two at a time.

questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single line and hold the handrail.

questions.question: When you approach a bus stop, students on your bus should:

options.text: Walk to the front of the bus to get ready to exit.

questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until the driver tells them to move. It is not safe for students to walk around while the bus is moving.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked unattended, you should:

options.text: Look for any animals that may be inside.

questions.explanation: Unattended buses can be damaged by people. Before driving an unattended bus, walk through the inside to check for any damage.

questions.question: Near a school with students present, can a driver back up if no helper is available?

options.text: Yes, but only if the path is clear.
Yes, but only at speeds under 10 mph.

questions.explanation: A bus cannot back up near a school when students are present unless a responsible person is there to guide the driver.

questions.question: Where are convex mirrors located on a school bus?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are placed below flat mirrors. They help the driver see a wide view of traffic, clearance, and students around the bus.

questions.question: What should a driver check before leaving a bus stop?

options.text: That no students are running to catch the bus.
That students have placed backpacks in the aisle.
That students have opened the emergency vent.
That students are facing the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: That no students are running to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Before pulling away from a bus stop, the driver must check that no students are running to board the bus.

questions.question: What should a driver do when unloading students at a school?

options.text: Turn off the ignition to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition and leave the driver's seat.
Read a book while students unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When dropping off students at a school, the driver must turn off the ignition to secure the bus. The driver should remove the key if they leave the driver's seat.

questions.question: Where should students go if a tornado is approaching and the bus is evacuated?
questions.explanation: If a tornado is sighted, the driver should lead students to shelter in a nearby building. If no building is available, move to a ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that flood and stay far enough away so the bus cannot fall on them.

questions.question: When must you back up at a student pick-up point, what should you do first?

options.text: Let all students board first, then back up.
Let half the students board, then back up toward the rest.
Tell students to wait, then back toward the stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let all students board first, then back up.
questions.explanation: If you must back up at a pick-up point, pick up all students first. When backing, watch carefully for students who may be running late.

questions.question: While the bus is moving, emergency exits should be:
questions.explanation: Emergency exits must be unlocked but firmly latched while the bus is moving.

questions.question: Why should a school bus stop at a distance from waiting students?

options.text: Students must walk to the bus, so the driver can watch them.
Students are usually on a sidewalk.
Students may be scared of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students must walk to the bus, so the driver can watch them.
questions.explanation: A school bus should stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students. This makes students walk to the bus, which helps the driver see and track their movements.

questions.question: Who should establish a school bus stop?

options.text: The driver can add stops as needed.
Stops can change based on weather.
School district authorities should establish stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: School district authorities should establish stops.
questions.explanation: A driver cannot change a bus stop location without written permission from school district officials.

questions.question: Buses must never carry ____ where passengers sit.
questions.explanation: Buses must never carry labeled radioactive materials in the area where passengers are seated.
